{{short description|American mathematician}}
'''Naomi G. Jochnowitz''' is an American mathematician interested in [[algebraic number theory]]. She is an associate professor of mathematics at the [[University of Rochester]].{{r|roch}}

Jochnowitz earned her Ph.D. in 1976 from [[Harvard University]]. Her dissertation, ''Congruences Between Modular Forms and Implications for the Hecke Algebra'', was supervised by [[Barry Mazur]].{{r|mgp}} At Rochester, she is known for her enthusiastic encouragement and support for incoming students to participate in the mathematics program, which contributed to a tripled number of mathematics majors from 1999 to 2002.{{r|integral}}

In 2016, Jochnowitz won the [[M. Gweneth Humphreys Award]] of the [[Association for Women in Mathematics]] for her mentorship of mathematics students and particularly of women in mathematics.{{r|humphreys}} She was also listed as a finalist for the "W" Award of the Rochester Women's Network for her mentorship of women in mathematics.{{r|w}} In 2018 she became one of the inaugural Fellows of the Association for Women in Mathematics.{{r|fawm}}
